2025_125_course_description_book_2024_20.paragraph: The 2025-2026 Course Descriptions catalog for Athens High School and Troy High School, published by the Troy School District under Superintendent Dr. Richard Machesky and revised in February 2025, lists course numbers, grade levels, semester length, credit values, retake rules, and prerequisites for every academic department at both buildings, plus Oakland Schools Technical Campus offerings. Graduation requires a total of 22.5 credits, including 4.0 English, 4.0 mathematics, 3.0 science, 3.0 social studies, and 3.0 combined World Language / Fine & Applied Arts / CTE. A 0.5-credit Personal Finance requirement embedded in Economics takes effect with the class of 2028.
2025_125_course_description_book_2024_20.page:
**Publication**
Troy School District course description book for the 2025-2026 school year, covering Athens High School and Troy High School. Dr. Richard Machesky, Superintendent of Schools. Revised February 2025. Athens High School: Mr. Vernon Burden, Principal, 4333 John R. Road, Troy, Michigan 48085. Troy High School: Mr. Remo Roncone, Principal, 4777 Northfield Parkway, Troy, Michigan 48098.

**Nondiscrimination**
Cites Title IX of the Educational Amendments of 1972, Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, and the Americans with Disabilities Act. Jordan M. Harris, J.D., Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services, is appointed Title IX and Section 504/ADA Coordinator for employment and personnel matters; the District's Director of Special Education serves as Section 504/ADA Coordinator for handicapped and suspected handicapped students. Contact listed as John Pagel, Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services, 4400 Livernois Road, Troy, MI 48098-4799, (248)823-4000.

**Graduation requirements**

| Area | Credits |
|---|---|
| English | 4.0 |
| Science | 3.0 |
| Mathematics | 4.0 |
| Social Studies | 3.0 |
| Personal Finance | 0.5 |
| Physical Education | 1.0 |
| Health | 0.5 |
| World Language, Fine & Applied Arts, CTE | 3.0 |
| Online Learning Experience | 0.0 |
| State Assessments | 0.0 |
| Total credits needed | 22.5 |

Science differs by cohort: the classes of '27, '28 and '29 take Biology 1.0, Chemistry 1 0.5, Physics 1 0.5, Environmental Science: Human Impact 0.5, and a 0.5 science elective; the class of '26 takes Biology 1.0, Chemistry OR Physics 1.0, and a 1.0 science elective. Personal Finance is embedded in Economics and becomes a requirement beginning with the class of 2028. The online learning requirement is a 20-hour non-credit experience.

**Flexibility options**
Updated 9.2015 under MCL 380.1278a and MCL 380.1278b. A Personal Curriculum allows substitution of additional core credits aligned to the student's Educational Development Plan. Two seasons of district athletics or marching band excuse the 0.5-credit physical education elective. The 2.0-credit World Language requirement may be flexed for heritage-language proficiency, international study, or substitution of CTE or Visual & Performing/Applied Arts credit. CTE program completion exchanges credits 1:1 for science, world language, or the Algebra 2 requirement.

**Career and Technical Education**
Programs listed are Architecture and Design; Automotive Technology; Business Administration, Management and Operations (BAMO); Computer Programming; Computer Information Systems and Security; Culinary Arts; Education; Finance; Marketing and Sales; Mechanical Drafting (Woodworking); Mechatronics; and Radio and Broadcasting Technology. Completers must take required courses in sequence; a grade of C or better makes a student eligible for an industry credential (Certiport, Microsoft Office Specialist, Intuit QuickBooks, ServSafe, ProStart, Child Development Associate).

**Departments covered**
Business; Information Technology; Education; Architecture & Mechanical Drafting; Mechatronics & Engineering; Automotive Technology; Radio and Broadcasting; Culinary Arts; Life Skills; English; English Language Development; Fine Arts (Visual Arts, Music, Theatre Arts); Health; Mathematics; Media; Multi-Departmental; Physical Education; Science; Social Studies; Special Education; and World Language (French, Spanish, Japanese, Chinese, German).

**Oakland Schools Technical Campus**
OSTC-SE, 5055 Delemere Street, Royal Oak, MI, north of 14 Mile between Crooks and Coolidge, grades 11-12. Course 08101 Session 1 AM (classes begin 7:50 AM, dismissed 10:20 AM) and 08102 Session 2 PM (begin 12:00 PM, dismissed 2:30 PM). Credit is generally 1.5 per semester. Applications are made online at www.ostconline.com by the end of February. OSTC credits are not NCAA approved.
2025_125_course_description_book_2024_20.verbose:
Troy School District's course description book for the 2025-2026 school year covers Athens High School and Troy High School and was revised in February 2025 under Dr. Richard Machesky, Superintendent of Schools. Athens High School is led by Mr. Vernon Burden, Principal, at 4333 John R. Road, Troy, Michigan 48085; Troy High School is led by Mr. Remo Roncone, Principal, at 4777 Northfield Parkway, Troy, Michigan 48098.

NONDISCRIMINATION AND GRIEVANCE. The opening policy statement cites Title IX of the Educational Amendments of 1972, Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, and the Americans with Disabilities Act. Jordan M. Harris, J.D., Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services, is appointed Title IX and Section 504/ADA Coordinator for employment and personnel matters, while the District's Director of Special Education is the Section 504/ADA Coordinator for handicapped and suspected handicapped students. Questions are directed to John Pagel, Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services, Troy School District, 4400 Livernois Road, Troy, MI 48098-4799, (248)823-4000. The Anti-Discrimination Grievance Procedure covers sex (including sexual harassment), race, color, religion, national origin, age (employees only), height, weight, marital status, and handicap. Step 1 requires a written grievance to the immediate supervisor within 10 workdays of the incident, with a copy to the Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services not later than the next workday, a meeting within 5 workdays of filing, and a written answer within 3 workdays of the meeting. Steps 2 and 3, to the Assistant Superintendent (or Deputy Superintendent) and then the Superintendent, each allow 3 workdays to appeal, 10 workdays to the meeting, and 5 workdays to a written answer; the Superintendent's decision is final and binding. Grievances not filed or appealed within the time limits are deemed abandoned.

GRADUATION REQUIREMENTS. Total credits needed for graduation is 22.5 for either a Troy High School or Troy Athens diploma. English requires 4.0 credits: English 9 (1.0), English 10 (1.0), English 11 Lit/Comp plus an English elective or 11 English AP 1 & 2 (1.0), and English 12 Lit/Comp 1 & 2 or 12 English AP 1 & 2 (1.0). Science requires 3.0 credits, with two cohort tracks: classes of '27, '28 and '29 take Biology 1.0, Chemistry 1 0.5, Physics 1 0.5, Environmental Science: Human Impact 0.5, and a science elective 0.5; the class of '26 takes Biology 1.0, Chemistry OR Physics 1.0, and a science elective 1.0. AP Environmental Science (1.0) can replace Environmental Science: Human Impact (0.5). Mathematics requires 4.0 credits: Algebra 1 (1.0), Geometry (1.0), Algebra 2 or Algebra 2 Part A plus Part B (1.0, or met through CTE program completion such as OSTC), and a math elective (1.0), with a math experience required in the final year. Social Studies requires 3.0 credits: World History/Geography 1 & 2 (1.0, with AP Human Geography fulfilling 0.5 of World History 1), American History/Geography 1 & 2 (1.0), Economics (0.5), and Government and Civics (0.5). Personal Finance is 0.5 credit embedded into Economics and becomes a graduation requirement beginning with the class of 2028. Physical Education requires 1.0 (Intro to Physical Activity 0.5 plus a PE elective 0.5); Health requires 0.5. The World Language / Fine & Applied Arts / CTE block requires 3.0 credits: 2.0 World Language (non-sequential accepted) or 1.0 World Language plus 1.0 CTE or 1.0 Visual, Performing or Applied Arts, plus 1.0 VPAA. A 20-hour online learning experience and completion of State of Michigan assessments are non-credit requirements. Flexibility options, updated 9.2015 under MCL 380.1278a and MCL 380.1278b, include the Personal Curriculum, an automated physical education waiver for two seasons of district athletics or marching band, world language flexibility, and 1:1 CTE credit exchange.

CTE PROGRAMS. The programs listed are Architecture and Design; Automotive Technology; Business Administration, Management and Operations (BAMO); Computer Programming; Computer Information Systems and Security; Culinary Arts; Education; Finance; Marketing and Sales; Mechanical Drafting (Woodworking); Mechatronics; and Radio and Broadcasting Technology. Completers must take courses in sequential order, with a C or better making them eligible for an industry credential.

BUSINESS. BAMO courses are 005231 Business Entrepreneurship, 005404 Digital Business, and 005415 Business Law & Management, with Certiport Entrepreneurship and Small Business (ESB) certification worth two ACE credits and a Communication Career Skills AI certification worth one ACE credit. The Finance and Accounting program lists 005011 Financial Accounting 1, 005012 Financial Accounting 2, and 005124 Building Wealth & Investments (formerly Financial Management), each satisfying 0.5 credit of the math-related graduation requirement in the 12th grade year. Marketing and Sales lists 005257 Marketing 1, 005258 Advanced Marketing, 005182 Sports and Entertainment Marketing, 005259 Marketing Research Capstone, and 105113/205113 School Based Enterprise (12th grade only). Work-Based Learning includes 105023/205023 Business Field Study (Co-op), 105213/205213 Marketing Field Study, and 108844/208844 Business Internship, each offering up to 2.0 credits for at least 10 hours per week and 200 hours per semester; unpaid internships must not exceed 45 hours per specific training experience.

INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY AND OTHER CTE. Computer Programming lists 103163/203163 AP Computer Science A and 103373/203373 Computer Science Principles AP; Cybersecurity is 003172 at Troy High and 103172/203172 at Athens. Digital Multimedia lists 005272 Web Creation 1, 005282 Web Page Creation 2, 007122 Game Design 1, and 007102 Game Design 2, all at Athens. Education lists 107393/207393 Careers in Education 1 and 107403/207403 Careers in Education 2, both held at Athens with placements in the Troy Athens Preschool; advanced placement credits are offered at Central University, Western Michigan University, Oakland University, Macomb Community College, and Davenport University, and completers of both courses are eligible for a Child Development Associate (CDA) credential. Architecture lists 007072 and 007082 Architectural Drawing 1 and 2; Mechanical Drafting & Woodworking lists 107163/207163 and 107173/207173 Woodworking Design & Fabrication 1 and 2. Mechatronics lists 108714/208714 Engineering & Advanced Manufacturing and 108724/208724 Engineering & Digital Manufacturing Systems. Automotive Technology, held at Troy High, lists 107003/207003 Auto Tech 1, 107294/207294 Auto Tech 2 (1 credit per semester, 2-hour block, 2 retakes), 107213/207213 Auto Tech 3, and 107413/207413 Auto Tech 4, with instruction meeting NATEF Automotive Maintenance and Light Repair standards. Radio and Broadcasting lists 000342 Writing for Broadcasting and 000362 Advanced Writing for Broadcasting. Culinary Arts, held at Athens, lists 107384/207384 Restaurant Operations / Terrace Cafe (2 hours, 2 credits), 107373/207373 Commercial Baking, and 107473/207473 Commercial Foods, using the ProStart curriculum with ServSafe Food Handler and ServSafe Manager credentials.

OTHER DEPARTMENTS. Life Skills includes 007242 and 007262 Parenthood/Child Development 1 and 2 (eligible for advanced placement credit at Oakland Community College), 009862 Essential Skills for Adulthood (described as Adulting 101), 007272 Personal Money Management, Foods and Culture, Foods 2, Fashion Design 1 and 2, Stitchery, and 007283 Interior Design/CAD. English offerings run from 101043/201043 English 9 through 100453/200453 12 English AP 1 & 2, plus electives including Creative Writing, Classical Mythology and Drama, Film and Literature, Graphic Novels, Literature of Suspense, Science Fiction, Voices in Literature, Sports Literature, Speech, Debate, Modern Shakespeare, and Writing for Publication in Journalism, Newspaper and Yearbook; AP Research culminates in a paper of approximately 4000-5000 words. English Language Development placement follows the State of Michigan Entrance Protocol with annual WIDA ACCESS testing, offering Beginner, Intermediate and Advanced ELD, Bridges to Lit/Comp for ELs, and EL Tutorial. Fine Arts spans visual art from 006212 Multi-Media Art through 106393/206393 Advanced Art AP; music ensembles including Campus, Concert, Cadet and Symphonic Band, Jazz Ensemble, Color Guard, Percussion, Freshman, Concert, Symphony and Philharmonic Orchestras, Treble Choir, Mixed Chorus, Concert Choir and Madrigal Singers, plus 106553/206553 Music Theory and 006501 Intro to Music Technology and Recording using ProTools; and Theatre I, II, III and Youth Theatre. Health (008852) is required for graduation. Mathematics ranges from Algebra 1 and 103123/203123 Intensified Algebra 1 (double-blocked two-hour course, 1 credit per semester) through Calculus AB AP, Calculus BC AP, Statistics AP, 103383/203383 Introduction to Data Science, 003145 Data Structures and Algorithms, and dual-enrollment 003212 Calculus 3 and 003222 Linear Algebra through Lawrence Tech. Physical Education includes 007952 and 007962 Intro to Physical Activity Levels 1 and 2, Net Sports, Team Sports & Fitness, Weight Training and Aerobics, Strength and Conditioning, and 005522 Lifeguarding/Advanced Swimming, which requires students to be 15 years old and carries a $40 certification cost. Social Studies includes AP Human Geography, American History/Geography covering the United States from 1877, Economics AP, Government AP, World History/Geography AP, Psychology AP, 002042 Comparative Government and Politics AP built around China, Great Britain, Iran, Mexico, Nigeria and Russia, 106383/206383 AP Art History covering 250 works of art, and 002617 Stories of Yourself & Others, worth 0.5 ELA credit and 0.5 History credit. Special Education (Central Office, 248.823.5096) lists Integrated Studies, Linguistics 9 through Linguistics and Composition 12, Reading Strategies, Integrated Math 1 and 2, English Language Arts 1 and 2, Math Skills A/B, Life Skills Math, and LS-designated sections of core academic subjects. World Language offers French, Spanish, Japanese, Chinese and German levels 1 through 4 with AP in French, Spanish, Japanese and Chinese, all keyed to ACTFL Proficiency Guidelines; Japanese 2 covers 120 basic Kanji, Japanese 3 another 170+ and Japanese 4 another 180+.

OAKLAND SCHOOLS TECHNICAL CAMPUS. OSTC-SE is at 5055 Delemere Street, Royal Oak, MI, north of 14 Mile between Crooks and Coolidge, serving grades 11-12 through 08101 Session 1 AM and 08102 Session 2 PM. Morning classes begin at 7:50 AM and are dismissed at 10:20 AM; afternoon classes begin at 12:00 PM and are dismissed at 2:30 PM. OSTC recommends high school credit at generally 1.5 credits per semester; if regular students carry six (6) credits, OSTC students must carry three (3) credits at their home high school in addition to three (3) at OSTC. Southeast Campus programs include Automotive Technology (must begin in 11th grade), Collision Repair and Refinishing, Computer Programming, Computer Networking, Construction Technology, Culinary Arts/Hospitality, Electrical and Energy Technologies, Entrepreneurship & Advanced Marketing, Health Sciences, Machining, Mechatronics, Visual Imaging Technology, Welding, and Homeland Security (Criminal Justice or Cyber Security); the Northeast Campus in Pontiac offers Cosmetology, which must begin in 11th grade. Applications are submitted online at www.ostconline.com by the end of February, buses are provided, and OSTC credits are not NCAA approved. The book closes with contact information for the Department of Teaching & Learning at 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.5221, and building numbers including 248.823.2900 and 248.823.2700 main offices, 248.823.2913 and 248.823.2713 fax, 248.823.2962 and 248.823.2715 counseling, and 248.823.2901 and 248.823.2701 attendance.
